acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Orcs family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Grunt, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Committed Shoulder-Tester (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two normal construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Lean and sinewy with hide wraps, small blunt tusks, almost no iron, and one crude spear or hand axe held close to the body.

Signature mechanic: Shoulder Test: the Grunt lowers one hide-wrapped shoulder behind its crude weapon and drives straight through the first occupied space; contact shoves both combatants, while a miss carries the Grunt past the target before it can turn.
battlefieldDuty: Probe the front line with a short spear or hand-axe rush that displaces a guarded target but leaves the lean attacker stranded if the rush misses.
constructionDimensions: Materials remain mundane and clan-marked: scarred grey-green skin, boiled leather, dark fur, riveted iron, crude steel, bone trophies, and mineral war paint show physical wear and repair.

Motion and surface effects stay bodily and mechanical: shifting weight, flexing leather, iron scrape, breath, sweat, kicked dust, and flaking paint reveal attack commitment without supernatural residue.
counterplay: Step across the narrow line rather than retreating, then strike the unarmored ribs or back while the Grunt plants its forward foot and turns. Affinity signal: War paint, planted feet, drawn-back shoulders, weapon arcs, banner ropes, and exposed armor joins preserve the mechanic-specific tells and recovery windows of every form.
forbiddenTreatments: Elemental spectacle that replaces tusks, scars, heavy weapons, or clan-marked equipment
identityInvariants: Tall, broad, top-heavy humanoid silhouette with a thick neck, wide shoulders, heavy jaw, forward lean, and lower tusks rising past the lip.
Grey-green or ash-grey skin is framed by blood red, black, dark iron, bone white, and readable red or white war paint.
Boiled leather, fur, riveted iron, bone, and crude steel remain thick, weighty, and practical rather than elegant or finely matched.
Scars, paint, tusk rings, piercings, skull trophies, spiked pauldrons, and clan totems communicate earned encounter rank without becoming a biological claim.
Tusk length, muscle mass, posture, and carried trophies escalate together, but every form retains committed heavy motion and exposed recovery as the family combat grammar.
telegraph: It scrapes one bare foot backward, tucks its small blunt tusks, and draws the spear or axe tight beside the lowered shoulder.
